# Indian Curry Techniques

## Building the Spice Foundation

Authentic Indian curries start with whole spices bloomed in hot oil. Mustard seeds, cumin seeds,
cardamom pods, cinnamon sticks, and dried red chiles are added to the pan and fried briefly until
fragrant. This technique, called a tarka or tadka, extracts fat-soluble flavor compounds from
the spices that water-based cooking cannot achieve.

## Aromatics and Base

After blooming the whole spices, add finely chopped onion and cook slowly over medium heat until
deeply caramelized to a golden brown color. This can take 20 to 30 minutes but forms the sweet
backbone of the curry. Add fresh ginger and garlic paste and cook until the raw smell dissipates.

## Ground Spice Mixture

Add the powdered spice blend: turmeric, coriander, cumin, and Kashmiri red chile powder for color.
Cook the ground spices in the oil with the onion paste for two minutes to remove rawness.
The mixture should pull away from the pan and the oil should separate and pool on the surface,
indicating the masala is properly cooked.

## Protein and Simmering

Add the protein (chicken, lamb, paneer, or legumes) and coat with the spice base.
Add tomatoes, fresh or canned, and simmer until they break down into a thick sauce.
Add water or stock to achieve desired consistency. Simmer covered for 20 to 40 minutes.
Finish with garam masala and fresh cilantro just before serving.

## Dal and Legume Curries

Lentil dal is cooked separately until very soft, then combined with a tarka of aromatics.
Red lentils (masoor dal) cook in 20 minutes. Black lentils (urad dal) take two to three hours
and benefit from overnight soaking to soften the skins.
